registryPurpose: Plan a registry-discovered visual tool suite so Flipbook, Sticker/Picture Book, Particle FX, and future Audio viewers load assets from reviewed manifests and pantry records instead of hardcoded paths or human memory.

userHeldDownloadsPrototypes.title: Sprite Box Annotator
userHeldDownloadsPrototypes.plannedRole: manual region/box annotation and future Sticker/Picture Book authoring helper

notes: Existing flipbook HTML files are evidence prototypes, not a canonical app surface.
Downloads prototypes were inspected for identity only and were not copied, moved, modified, or ingested.
Future tool implementation should harvest useful patterns through explicit approved intake, not by silently depending on Downloads paths.

toolSurfaces.purpose: Preview animation sheets and state/pose sequences from reviewed animation manifests without implying runtime approval.
requiredMetadata: direction or state tags if available
safetyBoundaries: No animation runtime approval.
No hitbox, hurtbox, pivot, baseline, gameplay-state, or timing approval unless a later manifest explicitly provides it.
State-symbol sets such as Ember Pup must not be mislabeled as approved animation cycles.
toolSurfaces.runtimeApprovalPolicy: Preview only until a later runtime asset manifest explicitly promotes a sequence.
toolSurfaces.recommendedFirstImplementationLane: H5.88A or later - consolidate existing flipbook evidence into a registry-fed viewer

toolSurfaces.purpose: Preview static regions, cleaned candidates, backgrounds, scene anchors, UI/card surfaces, tiles, walls, objects, and placement planning metadata through the pantry registry.
safetyBoundaries: Accepted cleaned assets are not automatically valid scene placements.
Denied/deferred/visual-only status must remain visible.
No collision, placement, tilemap, card behavior, pickup, chest, trap, portal, or gameplay approval from display alone.
toolSurfaces.runtimeApprovalPolicy: Viewer may display draft/reviewed assets, but runtime use remains blocked until a later runtime-specific promotion manifest exists.
toolSurfaces.recommendedFirstImplementationLane: H5.88B or later - registry-fed static asset viewer/picture book shell

toolSurfaces.purpose: Preview particle presets and adjustable procedural effects that can replace many deferred glow/fire/smoke/portal sprite cleanup risks.
safetyBoundaries: Particle presets are visual presets only until runtime wiring.
No automatic gameplay behavior.
No damage, light, collision, portal, weather, status, or feedback behavior approval.
Shared FX remains particle-first/reference-only until concrete needs produce approved presets.
toolSurfaces.runtimeApprovalPolicy: No runtime behavior until a future FX runtime manifest explicitly promotes a preset.
toolSurfaces.recommendedFirstImplementationLane: Future H5/H6 tooling lane after visual registry is accepted

toolSurfaces.purpose: Reserve future audio pipeline scope without mixing audio into the Tier 1.5 visual asset registry.
safetyBoundaries: Audio is future Tier 2.5.
No audio implementation or runtime triggers in H5.88.
Do not mix audio readiness into visual runtime approval.
toolSurfaces.runtimeApprovalPolicy: Future-only; no audio runtime approval in Tier 1.5.

unsupportedOrFutureAssetTypes.reason: Runtime approval requires later H6+ integration manifests and is not granted by the tool registry.
Audio is future Tier 2.5 and is only reserved in H5.88.
3D asset canonical pose and runtime gates belong to a separate future pipeline.
Tools should discover through pantry and manifest records, not arbitrary folder scans.

rules: Tools read from a registry/pantry manifest before loading individual assets.
Tools must not hardcode random source paths.
Tools must preserve accepted, denied, deferred, historical, future-pantry-only, and needs-human-review statuses.
Tools must visibly display pipelineUse, reviewStatus, runtimeEligibility, and denial/defer reasons.
Tools may read source/derived/evidence paths from manifests, but display is not approval.
Downloads-held prototypes are references only until explicitly ingested.

safetyBoundaries: H5.88 is planning only.
No tools are built.
No runtime wiring is approved.
No game code is changed.
No PNGs are changed.
No manifests or docs are reorganized.
No collision, pathfinding, placement, tilemap, animation behavior, particle behavior, or audio behavior is approved.
Button Goblin Clicker remains the first later runtime visual integration candidate.
Top-Down Slime Quest remains last or near-last for runtime visual integration.

openQuestions: Should the Downloads-held Sprite Box Annotator and Particle FX Viewer be ingested as canonical repo prototypes, archived as references, or regenerated as cleaner repo-native tools?
Should the first unified tool surface be a single HTML launcher, a Vite/React page, or a script-generated static evidence viewer?
Should tool discovery use the current pantry index directly or a new derived tool registry emitted from the pantry index?
Where should future tool implementation live: scripts/asset-pipeline, tools/glyphforge, docs/assets/tooling, or a dedicated app surface?
How much of the existing evidence flipbook code should be reused versus replaced by a registry-fed viewer?
notes: H5.88 maps the tool bench; it does not build the bench.
The pantry index remains the Tier 1.5 source of truth.
H5.87 remains the shelf organization plan.
Audio is acknowledged only as future Tier 2.5.
